description.narrative:
Project Equal Care seeks to improve access to inclusive, youth-friendly health services for adolescent girls and young women (AGYW)with disabilities in Lagos State. The project will empower AGYW with disabilities to take on leadership roles, engage in policy advocacy, and contribute to health service reforms that prioritize their needs.
Firstly, the project will strengthen the advocacy capacity of AGYW with disabilities by developing a policy brief on the key barriers to accessing youth-friendly health services. This brief will include evidence-based recommendations and be shared with key stakeholders to raise awareness and drive policy change. Secondly, the project will foster collaboration through a roundtable discussion with policymakers, civil society, and youth-led organizations. This platform will present the policy brief’s findings and work towards actionable strategies to improve healthcare access for AGYW with disabilities. Thirdly, the project will provide capacity-building training on sexual reproductive health and rights (SRHR) advocacy, leadership, and storytelling to young female policy influencers chosen from the youth parliament, youth council, and youth ambassadors, including AGYW with disabilities. These trainings will equip participants to effectively advocate for inclusive policies and health services.
Fourthly, a mentorship program will pair AGYW with disabilities with young female policy influencers, fostering peer learning and providing practical insights into navigating advocacy and policy-making spaces. Lastly, the project will ensure that AGYW with disabilities have a tangible impact by supporting their participation in advocacy and decision-making events. Through advocacy visits to key policymakers and by engaging AGYW with disabilities in national or local discussions, the project willensure that their voices are heard in the development of inclusive health policies.
Through these integrated efforts, Project Equal Care will create a more equitable healthcare system for AGYW with disabilities, amplifying their voices and ensuring their active participation in shaping policies that affect their health and rights.

participating-org.narrative:
SID Initiative is a youth-led, female-led, and youth-serving non-governmental organization founded in April 2019 and dedicated to advancing the sexual reproductive health and well-being of adolescents and young people in urban and rural communities in Nigeria. Our mission is to empower young people to lead healthy lives by providing sexual and reproductive health and rights information and services through comprehensive sexuality education, capacity building, advocacy, and digital innovation. Our vision is a society whereevery young person's health and development is realized. Our values are teamwork, integrity, empathy, sustainability and evidence. Our target group includes adolescent girls and young women (AGYW) living with HIV, AGYW with disabilities, AGYW in rural areas, and adolescents and young people out-of-school and in-school.
Our organization operates under a governance structure that ensures inclusive and participatory decision-making. The leadership team consists of seven young women below the age of 35 who actively lead the planning, implementation, and monitoring of all programs and initiatives. We also have a pool of 30 volunteers who support the planning and implementation of our programs. This ensures that our work remains youth-driven, responsive, and aligned with the needs of our target communities.
Our Board of Trustees, composed entirely of women (six members), provides strategic oversight and guidance. Notably, 50% of the board members are under the age of 35, reinforcing ourcommitment to youth leadership while balancing experience and expertise. The governance framework is structured to foster accountability, transparency, and efficiency, with clear roles, procedures, and responsibilities guiding decision-making processes.
